# Reading a filing cadence

> When did they last file accounts, and what has been filed since?

Filing history is the closest thing on the register to a timeline. Accounts give the year end and the size bracket a company files under; mortgage filings show when it borrowed; officer filings show when people arrived and left.

> **About the responses below.** They are real output from this server — every
> call on this page is executed when the documentation is generated, and
> whatever comes back is what you see. The upstream data comes from fixtures
> recorded from the live Companies House API, so the companies are real and
> the facts are public record, published under the Open Government Licence
> v3.0. The framing around them is illustrative: this project makes no claim
> about any company or person named here beyond what the register itself
> states.

## Walkthrough

### 1. get_filing_history

Pull the recent history. Filter by category when only one kind of event matters.

```json
{
  "tool": "get_filing_history",
  "arguments": {
    "company_number": "04138203",
    "items_per_page": 5
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "company_number": "04138203",
  "filings": [
    {
      "date": "2026-02-03",
      "category": "officers",
      "subcategory": "termination",
      "type": "TM01",
      "description": "termination-director-company-with-name-termination-date",

        "termination_date": "2026-01-30"
      },
      "pages": 1,
      "has_document": true
    },
    {
      "date": "2026-01-22",

      "subcategory": "appointments",
      "type": "AP01",
      "description": "appoint-person-director-company-with-name-date",
      "description_values": {
        "officer_name": "Mr Paul Ablin",
        "appointment_date": "2026-01-21"
      },
      "pages": 2,
      "has_document": true
    },
    {
      "date": "2025-12-22",
      "category": "accounts",
      "type": "AA",
      "description": "accounts-with-accounts-type-full",
      "description_values": {
        "made_up_date": "2025-03-30"
      },
      "pages": 74,
      "has_document": true
    },
    {

      "category": "confirmation-statement",
      "type": "CS01",
      "description": "confirmation-statement-with-updates",
      "description_values": {
        "made_up_date": "2025-11-11"
      },
      "pages": 4,
      "has_document": true
    },
    {
      "date": "2025-08-20",
      "category": "officers",
      "subcategory": "appointments",
      "type": "AP01",
      "description": "appoint-person-director-company-with-name-date",
      "description_values": {
        "officer_name": "Mr Dwain Mcdonald",
        "appointment_date": "2025-08-01"
      },
      "pages": 2,
      "has_document": true
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "start_index": 0,
    "items_per_page": 5,
    "total_results": 284,
    "returned": 5,
    "has_more": true
  },
  "meta": {
    "cached": false,
    "stale": false,
    "rate_limit_remaining": 569,
    "rate_limit_resets_in_ms": 0,
    "licence": "OGL-v3.0"
  }
}
```

`description` is a Companies House template key such as `accounts-with-accounts-type-full`, with the values that fill it alongside. It is not translated into English here on purpose: rendering it properly needs a template file Companies House ships separately, and a partial local translation would render some filings wrongly with nobody able to tell which.

The key is informative in itself — `accounts-type-full` is a company filing full accounts rather than the abridged or micro-entity form.

`has_document` says a filed document exists. Fetching the PDF needs the separate Companies House document API, which is out of scope for this server today.

## Notes

**For a running watch,** the cache TTLs are what to know: filing history is cached for six hours, the shortest of any section, because it is what changes when anything happens. Set `CH_CACHE_ENABLED=false` if you need this second's answer.
